title: Reel — the video modules, one at a time
stage: VR1: field shapes videoMaths timeMachine compositor videoOut

steps.note: This demo will highlight a few features of DreamRack video synthesis. We will also see how to modulate video with a normal audio control voltage.

steps.say: Let's go to the video page.

steps.note: These are some of the basic video modules, left to right in the order they are normally used. We'll learn a bit about each and build a video patch.
Video Output, at the right hand end. Every video chain finishes here. Even without input it can show the test pattern you see here.
You can open the output into a larger window, make it full screen, or open it on a different monitor. Let's open it on the right.
Coordinate Field, at the far end, and it's the workhorse of the set. It owns a coordinate space and does two things with it: it moves that space, and it reads a value out of it as brightness.
Patch it straight to the output, replacing the test pattern.

Radius gives us distance from the centre of the frame, drawn as brightness. The coordinate module gives us a soft gradient, so there isn't much to see with it alone. We'll bring in the next module before touching any of these knobs.
Shapes. It takes a field and keeps a slice of it, and that's how you get something with an edge out of something that's all gradient.

steps.after: And the chain is three modules long.

steps.note: Width is how much of the field we keep. Narrow it down and what's left is a thin ring.
Centre is where in the field that slice sits, so on a radius field it moves the ring in and out.
Open the width right up and the ring fills in to a disc. One control gives you both, which is why there's no shape switch.
And it isn't only rings. The mode switch keeps everything above the slice instead of the slice itself, which turns the same field into an edge rather than a band.
Narrow it back a little and that edge gets a soft band of its own.
Set low, the edge sits near the middle of the field.
And soft turns the cut into a gradient, which is what you want when the shape is going to meet something else rather than be looked at on its own.
Now we have an edge to watch, the coordinate field's own controls are worth going back to. Every one of them moves the space that edge is cut out of.
Scale zooms that space. Far enough out and there's nothing left in the frame, which is the honest thing a zoom does.
So we come back in, past where we started, until the whole of it is in view.
Tile repeats the space across the frame. One shape becomes a row of them, and it costs nothing — the same field is simply read more than once.
Quantise steps the field into bands instead of a smooth run, and that's what turns a gradient into hard-edged rings.
Twist turns the space further the further out you go, so the bands wind round each other.
Rotate turns the whole thing.
And polar is a sweep rather than a switch, so a little of it bends the grid without going all the way round.

Scroll is the one that makes it move. It drifts what's read out of the space, half a frame a second, and nothing is patched to do it — the video is running on its own now, out of two modules and two cables.
